body: It's a bug, fixing it now.

BTW - I think `utf8_encode()` in https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/base/Security.php#L301 is not applicable as random data are returned by `generateRandomKey`

See http://php.net/manual/en/function.utf8-encode.php#104906

> Please note that utf8_encode only converts a string encoded in ISO-8859-1 to UTF-8...
> In fact, applying this function to text that is not encoded in ISO-8859-1 will most likely simply garble that text.

Yes, there is a change in the result of `generateRandomKey()` which is now a binary string rather than an ASCII string. We may need an enhancement to still support ASCII string, but I don't know how to do it correctly.

The code about `utf8_encode()` is mainly to allow `json_encode()` the secret keys. When the secret key is returned, `utf8_decode()` is called to ensure the original binary key is returned.
nope, that would prevent you from directly modifying `keys.json`.

I really want to see that `generateRandomKey()` has an option to generate a key containing ASCII chars only. Binary strings sometimes are troublesome to deal with, like in this case and when you want to store the key in DB. @klimov-paul any idea?
Also one could use `bin2hex(Yii::$app->security->generateRandomKey(16))`. It will generate 32 characters long string.

> The following generates random string safe to use in URLs:

Is it cryptographically correct to do so?
Not really since there are replacements. `bin2hex` is correct though.
Should we add an option `hexDigitsOnly` then?

![twijo1ka](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/2150916/3423874/9c0d1214-ffaf-11e3-8a20-ac50f0ebec88.png)

1 - generated by old security manager
2 - `utf8_encode(Yii::$app->security->generateRandomKey())`
3 - `bin2hex(Yii::$app->security->generateRandomKey(16))`

Seems that the 1-st looks stronger than the 3-rd (more letters are used and in upper and lower case).
@SDKiller that's just representation of exactly the same data.
Yeah, as you see the hex representation is longer to store but strenght is the same.
@qiangxue I'd prefer separate method `generateRandomString` rather than option.
Actually not since it can't generate string of a certain length.
